events.title: The Pardon of Assisi
events.shortBlurb: The great indulgence tradition holds St. Francis obtained for pilgrims to the little chapel of the Portiuncula…
body: The Portiuncula, the 'little portion', was a ruined chapel of St. Mary of the Angels below Assisi, given to Francis and his first brothers by the Benedictines of Monte Subasio. Francis rebuilt it with his own hands and made it the home of his young order; here in 1212 he received Clare and cut her hair, and here he died on 3 October 1226.

Here, by a tradition the Franciscan sources fix in 1216, the Pardon of Assisi began. Praying one night, Francis saw Christ and his Mother amid a host of angels and asked that all who entered the little church, repentant and confessed, might receive full pardon of their sins. He hastened to Pope Honorius III, then at Perugia, who granted the unheard-of gift of a plenary indulgence.

The indulgence could be gained in the chapel from first vespers of 1 August to sunset of 2 August, as is still kept; later popes extended the Pardon, under the usual conditions of confession, Communion, and prayer for the pope's intentions, to parish churches everywhere. The little chapel itself stands enshrined today within the basilica of St. Mary of the Angels, raised from 1569 to shelter it.
